A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AICoG research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-D. Content can be matched reliably despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original link-prediction, node-classification, and subcompositional evaluation results.

after.justification: The original empirical results remain, supplemented by synthetic membership recovery, Cora membership diagnostics, and quantitative single-balance analyses.

M1.justification: The softmax compositions, ILR embeddings, fixed and learned bases, Bernoulli latent-distance likelihood, and subcomposition procedure are unchanged. The explicit distance formula and expanded proof do not introduce an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same seven real-world networks. v3 adds ground-truth membership recovery on synthetic graphs crossing continuous versus near-discrete memberships with bilinear versus ILR-distance generators, introducing a distinct evaluation task and four controlled scenarios.

E2.justification: Matched experiments retain NODE2VEC, ROLE2VEC, NETMF, SLIM-RAA, MMSBM, MNMF, HM-LDM, and SIMPLEX-EUCLIDEAN. The added synthetic and membership-overlap comparisons reuse MMSBM; no comparator is added or removed from the retained comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 adds a crossed synthetic evaluation design with L1 distance, cosine similarity, and Jensen-Shannon divergence, plus membership-interiority metrics, raw-membership classifiers, and single-balance probes. Existing edge holdouts, embedding dimensions, benchmark metrics, and optimization budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained basis visualizations, trade-off trajectories, and component-removal tests, v3 adds analyses of ground-truth membership recovery, overlapping versus near-corner representations, and label information in individual balances. These substantially expand direct testing of the representation's claimed properties.

E5.justification: v3 introduces an ANOVA F-statistic as a statistical assessment of balance-label separation, without reporting a p-value. Existing five-run averages, 50-mask averaging, and the statement that variance around 10^-3 is omitted remain unchanged. No additional run counts or uncertainty estimates accompany the new analyses.

E6.justification: All retained benchmark values match, including v1 Tables 4-5, renumbered 6-7 in v3. New Table 4 reports better membership recovery for AICoG than MMSBM in all four settings; Table 5 reports Cora membership-probe accuracy of 0.670 versus 0.306. Newly reported single-balance results include approximately 0.40 accuracy, F=319, and mutual information 0.44.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.2 explicitly specifies a fixed valid ILR basis, and Appendix A adds a constructive inverse and proofs of surjectivity and injectivity. v1 assumed bijectivity in its shorter proof. The expressive-equivalence conclusion and subcomposition theorem are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, five introductory contributions, and principal conclusion retain the same claims about compositional interpretability, Euclidean expressive equivalence, component restriction, and competitive prediction. The added experiments supply evidence without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the added diagnostics as showing label-informative membership overlap and meaningful individual balances. Section 5 newly qualifies the evidence as primarily covering connected or dominant-component graphs and discusses disconnected graphs as future work. The underlying geometric interpretation and non-identifiability qualification already existed.

D1.justification: v3 removes Section 4's statement that code is supplied as supplementary material and will be released publicly, while retaining the same public repository link in the abstract. Hardware, optimization settings, and Appendix C implementation details are unchanged; the new analyses lack corresponding detailed setup specifications.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work discussion are unchanged. The positioning relative to Euclidean embeddings, mixed-membership models, and post-hoc explanation methods remains the same.

P1.justification: v3 adds a three-level explanation of interpretability, compacts the contribution list, clarifies mathematical exposition, and corrects local wording and notation. Affiliations, acknowledgments, and running headers are updated, while the overall section structure and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 4-5, reduces Table 3 to a single-column display, and redistributes existing figures and appendix tables. Figure 1 corrects 'Inverse Log Ratio' to 'Isometric Log Ratio' and adjusts typography. Figures 2-4 retain their plotted evidence.

improvement.justification: The new membership and balance analyses provide more direct quantitative support for the compositional interpretation, while Appendix A makes ILR bijectivity explicit and Section 5 clarifies an applicability boundary. These are useful gains, but the added experiments lack synthetic-generation, membership-alignment, probe-split, and uncertainty details, limiting reproducibility and the strength of the additional evidence. The method and original benchmark findings remain unchanged.
